newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador energy minister tells VP to stay home.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador energy minister tells VP to stay home.

text.p: Ecuadoran Energy Minister Alfredo Adum, who said in a magazine interview last month that he wanted to run naked "like a caveman" and "devour" women, accused the vice president on Wednesday of plotting a coup and told her to stay at home.
Adum was apparently angry at Vice President Rosalia Arteaga for supporting a woman employee of state oil company Petroecuador who alleges that Adum punched her in the face.

Adum also criticised Arteaga for using the balcony of the presidential palace on Monday to address a crowd of 1,500 who had marched there to demand Adum's resignation because of his rough treatment of state gasoline workers.
"She is a coup plotter. She took the presidential balcony. Why? She can't go into the presidential palace, it's the private property of the president of the republic," he said.
"She's the vice president and her only hope is that if the president goes, she will be called to take his place. Until then she should stay at home," Adum told reporters.
